sections.name: researchWorkbook
sections.title: Building the workbook tabs
sections.what: Builds one row per project and one row per field in each group, marks each field as missing, not admitted, conflicting, partially supported or source reported, and returns the tabs and summary counts.
sections.why: Stated in the comment: raw wording is kept and no currency, unit or date conversion happens.
sections.watch_out: Conflict is judged on exact text, so two values that differ only in spacing or case are reported as conflicting.

summary: Builds the research workbook: a set of named tables, such as All Projects, Cost, Schedule and Sources, that show every claim, whether it was admitted, and which fields are missing.
purpose: Gives a readable tabbed view of run research. It keeps rejected claims visible and never converts units, currencies or dates.
why: Stated in the comment: this is the hosted equivalent of the directory, cost, schedule and snapshot tabs, and it keeps raw source wording.
how: First, for each project, list its identity, research status and fields with no admitted claim. Second, for each group of fields, give each field a status such as missing, not admitted, conflicting, partially supported or source reported, with all its reports. Third, build the tabs, including Value Chain, Segments, Sources, Verification and a Summary count.
inputs: The project record ledger, the research facts, and the project identity list with identifier, industry and sub-industry.
outputs: An object with a version, a notice, and named tabs, each a list of rows. The Summary tab holds counts of candidate, admitted and not admitted facts.
risks: Conflicts are judged on exact text, so values that differ only by spacing or capitals count as conflicting. A fact missing from the facts list counts as not admitted. Missing identity falls back to not recorded.
debug: If a tab is empty, check the project record. If a status looks wrong, check the admission result for each fact. In the Verification tab, the value legacy_not_rechecked means a fact has no assessment.
